title: Topics in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies; Feminist Disability Studies
description: This seminar is a feminist exploration of the interdisciplinary field of disability studies, questioning the definition of disability and who fits into the category. After introducing the field, classes will be organized around keywords in disability studies: language, technology, time, work, citizenship, and liberation. When we study language, we will read Sunaura Taylors scholarship in critical animal studies and multi-species justice. When we study work, we will learn that the jobs people do are often disabling. Our feminist and anti-racist analysis of labor will help us understand that the people are not equally likely to be working in dangerous jobs. And when we study time, we will examine and critique a range of imagined futures that exclude disability, that construct narrow visions of the good life, and promote limited rhetorics of self-improvement. Our course materials will include a variety of theory texts, accounts of personal experience, visual culture, and materials produced by organizers involved in direct action strategies.
